summary: Iter 12 — Full end-to-end validation of the Nubo Ride module (transporte de pasajeros). Backend: 7/7 tests in test_nubo_ride.py GREEN (estimate, full lifecycle, RBAC request/accept, customer cancel, duplicate-active validation, admin visibility). Frontend Playwright e2e (customer + rider in separate browser contexts): 16/16 steps GREEN — customer login → dashboard banner (nubo-ride-btn) → /ride → ride-form with origin/destination Selects → choose Algeciras → Barcelona → ride-estimate-btn → 3 vehicle cards rendered (ride-vehicle-economy/comfort/xl) with prices €1138.17 < €1575.33 < €2100.80 (>0 and correctly ordered) → select economy + ride-request-btn → ride-active-card visible with estado='Buscando conductor…' + ride-active-price=€1138.17 + ride-cancel-btn → duplicate POST /api/rides/request returns 400 'Ya tienes un viaje en curso' (single-active validation enforced server-side) → rider /rider activation with code NUBO-6NJP succeeds, rider-rides-section visible, rider-accept-ride-{id} button rendered → accept transitions ride to 'aceptado' and customer UI (after reload) shows 'Conductor en camino' → rider-ride-start → en_curso → customer UI shows 'Viaje en curso' AND ride-cancel-btn is correctly hidden during en_curso (matches code: estado !== 'en_curso') → rider-ride-complete → backend marks 'completado' → customer reload: ride-active-card disappears and ride-form reappears (active ride cleared). Suite total: 146/154 pytest passing (8 pre-existing failures in password-reset & businesses tests — unrelated to Nubo Ride scope; the preview is wired to nubo_produccion Atlas which lacks businesses seed and likely Resend env).

minor.issue: test_regression_modularization.test_get_businesses_public fails on prod Atlas DB (no businesses seeded). Pre-existing environmental — out of Nubo Ride scope.
6 password-reset tests fail in this preview (likely missing RESEND_API_KEY / network differences vs iter11 env). Out of Nubo Ride scope.

issues: Distance shown is straight-line geodesic (881.19 km / ETA 1718 min) which is huge for a passenger ride request; product may want to (a) restrict ride requests to same-region/short distances or (b) reflect a road-distance multiplier and cap. Cosmetic/product decision, not a bug — backend math is correct per haversine.

action_items: (Optional product polish) Consider warning the user when origin/destination are in different regions because the resulting fare is unrealistic for a single passenger ride (Algeciras→Barcelona = €1138.17). Backend computes haversine straight-line — this is intentional but UX-confusing for a 'Uber-like' service.

(Out of scope, but visible in full pytest run) 8 failing tests outside Nubo Ride: 6 password-reset + 2 businesses/orders — likely caused by preview pointing to Atlas prod DB (no businesses seeded) and possibly missing RESEND_API_KEY. Not blocking Nubo Ride.
critical_code_review_comments: rides.py implements proper atomic reclaim on accept via update_one with {estado:'buscando', conductor_id:None} filter — second concurrent accept correctly returns 409, validated in test_full_ride_lifecycle.

Regional isolation respected: accept_ride rejects 409/403 when ride.region_id != driver.region_id; available rides query in /rides/active for drivers limits to their region or region_id=None (cross-region public).
Duplicate-active validation enforced server-side (existing find_one with estado in ACTIVE_STATES) — frontend benefits but cannot be bypassed by manipulating UI. Verified with raw fetch in e2e step 7.
Cancel button correctly hidden in UI during 'en_curso' (NuboRide.js L317) — matches business rule that an in-progress ride cannot be cancelled by the client.
Polling on /api/rides/active every 5s while active ride is in buscando|aceptado|en_curso (NuboRide.js L80-85). useEffect cleanup correctly clears interval. No memory leak.
Money formatting helper handles MAD/EUR cleanly; currency derives from origin city's country (.country === 'MA'). GPS origin always defaults to EUR (acceptable simplification).
MongoDB _id always excluded via {_id:0} projections — no ObjectId leakage.

Telegram alert call (telegram_alerts.notify_new_ride) is awaited inline in /rides/request — could become latency burden if Telegram is slow; consider asyncio.create_task to avoid blocking the response. Low priority.

success_rate.backend: 100% Nubo-Ride scope (7/7), 94.8% overall suite (146/154 — 8 pre-existing failures unrelated to ride module)
